sentences.text: Arcticodactylus holds the record for the smallest known pterosaur, with an estimated wingspan of 24 cm.
Its jaws contained eleven or twelve multi-cusped teeth on each side.
The femur measured 96% of the tibia's length.
The scapula was much longer than the coracoid, measuring 93% of its length.
The humerus was slightly shorter than the femur at 92% of its length, and also 91% of the ulna's length.
The first wing finger phalanx measured 91% of the femoral length.
The third metatarsal of the foot was elongated, measuring 56% of the tibia's length.
These proportions imply that the animal had relatively short wings and large feet.
Analysis of its bone structure suggests the holotype was not a newborn but had not yet finished growing.
William Amaral discovered the fossil site in 1989 on McKnight Bjerg in eastern Greenland.
Farish Jenkins and colleagues named the species Eudimorphodon cromptonellus in 2001.
The species name cromptonellus honors Professor Alfred Walter Crompton.
Alexander Kellner established the separate genus Arcticodactylus in 2015.

Jenkins and colleagues proposed that the unique joint between the main wing metacarpal and the finger represented a transitional form between ancestors with a single rounded articular surface allowing considerable lateral movement and the condition of late pterosaurs showing a slight depression or trochlea.
Arcticodactylus belongs to the parent group Pterosauria.
The animal is classified in the class Reptilia.
The type species of the genus Arcticodactylus is Arcticodactylus cromptonellus.
A 2020 study by Matthew G. Baron grouped Arcticodactylus within the clade Caviramidae alongside Carniadactylus and Raeticodactylus.
In 2001, E. cromptonellus was placed in the family Eudimorphodontidae.
In 2015, Kellner indicated a basal position within Pterosauria and suggested a close affinity to Austriadraco within a family Austriadraconidae based on the short coracoid.
Arcticodactylus lived during the Late Triassic in what is now Greenland.
It is debated whether Arcticodactylus is closely related to Eudimorphodon, as researchers have noted it lacks key traits like fang-like teeth and striated enamel found in Eudimorphodon.
